description: Gate G48 on the TRNXFILE DD's first sequential READ, and the case that pins the READ ... INTO space-fill rule. The two CALLs scripted here are the caller's own idiom transcribed from app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:730-746: 8100-TRNXFILE-OPEN MOVEs 'TRNXFILE' TO WS-M03B-DD (:731), SETs M03B-OPEN TO TRUE (:732), MOVEs ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC (:733) and CALLs (:734); then - without moving the DD name again, and without re-zeroing a status the successful OPEN has already left at '00' - it SETs M03B-READ TO TRUE (:744), MOVEs SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT (:745) and CALLs again (:746). Two CALLs means two 1040-byte area images, pinned in call order, because the shared area is the whole observable behaviour of one CALL. The second call takes this path through app/cbl/CBSTM03B.CBL: the ordered EVALUATE LK-M03B-DD (:118) matches WHEN 'TRNXFILE' (:119) ahead of every later arm and performs 1000-TRNXFILE-PROC THRU 1999-EXIT (:120); inside that paragraph (:133) the first guard IF M03B-OPEN (:135) is now FALSE, so evaluation falls to IF M03B-READ (:140), which is TRUE: READ TRNX-FILE INTO LK-M03B-FLDT (:141) runs and GO TO 1900-EXIT (:143) transfers past the CLOSE guard (:146); 1900-EXIT (:151-152) then performs the unconditional MOVE TRNXFILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC and 1999-EXIT (:154-155) EXITs. That guard order is behaviour, not layout, and is preserved exactly (gate G30, rule R7) - reversing the two IFs would make the OPEN call read and the READ call open, and both calls would still return '00'. A successful sequential READ of an existing indexed dataset reports '00', and it reports it on the TRNXFILE-STATUS area specifically (gate G47), which is the only one of the four groups at :83-97 that 1900-EXIT moves from; the other three are untouched and this case claims nothing about them. READ ... INTO is a group MOVE into LK-M03B-FLDT PIC X(1000) (:112), so the alphanumeric receiving rule decides the result: the 350-byte record is placed left-justified and the remaining bytes are spaces, which is why LK-M03B-FLDT is pinned as bytes 1-350 of the record followed by exactly 650 spaces, and why neither side of the comparison is trimmed. Read order is ascending 32-byte TRNX-KEY, which is a property of the dataset rather than an assumption: app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL DELDEF01 DEFINEs the TRXFL cluster with KEYS(32 0) and RECORDSIZE(350 350), and STEP010 builds its content with SORT FIELDS=(263,16,CH,A,1,16,CH,A) - card number ascending, then transaction id ascending - so the first record a sequential READ delivers is the lower key 05000244537657400000000058866561 and not whichever row happens to come first in the source fixture. Both area images pin all six linkage spans by name and again as the complete image: LK-M03B-DD X(08) 'TRNXFILE', LK-M03B-OPER X(01) 'O' then 'R', LK-M03B-RC X(02) '00' both times, LK-M03B-KEY X(25) twenty-five spaces because a sequential READ passes no key, LK-M03B-KEY-LN S9(4) as the signed zoned image '000{' - a brace because the sign of a positive zero is overpunched into the low-order byte, and four zoned DISPLAY bytes rather than a two-byte halfword, which is what holds LK-M03B-FLDT at offset 40 - and LK-M03B-FLDT X(1000), still 1000 spaces after the OPEN because an OPEN delivers no record, then the record plus its padding after the READ. 8 + 1 + 2 + 25 + 4 + 1000 = 1040, re-derivable from the LINKAGE SECTION at :100-112 without tooling (practice B11). Both seeded rows are pinned unchanged afterwards, field by field across all fourteen app/cpy/COSTM01.CPY spans including the trailing FILLER X(20) whose twenty spaces carry the record's full width - 16 + 16 + 2 + 4 + 10 + 100 + 11 + 9 + 50 + 50 + 10 + 26 + 26 + 20 = 350 (gates G19 and G21). That is the read-only proof, and it is the reason the second row is pinned at all: every SELECT is OPEN INPUT and no paragraph of CBSTM03B contains a WRITE or a REWRITE, so a sequential READ advances a cursor and changes no byte of the dataset - it must not consume, reorder or blank the row it did not return. The unit is StatementGenerationJobB, whose prompt-mandated name is honoured verbatim under rule R1 while its nature is a Spring @Component and not a Spring Batch Job (gate G12, implicit requirement I3): the source header reads 'Type : BATCH COBOL Subroutine', no EXEC PGM=CBSTM03B exists anywhere in app/jcl, app/proc or app/csd, and CBSTM03A calls it thirteen times. The divergence is recorded rather than quietly resolved (practice B4). unitKind is therefore COMPONENT and the unit is reached through a typed method with no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path (gate G51), which is also why jobParameters is empty - a job parameter comes from a JCL PARM and this subroutine has no way to receive one. expectedReturnCode is 0 because CBSTM03B never assigns RETURN-CODE; the two-byte LK-M03B-RC is a FILE STATUS carried in the linkage area and the two are never conflated. expectedMessages is empty because CBSTM03B contains no DISPLAY statement at all - the diagnostic for this very operation, DISPLAY 'ERROR READING TRNXFILE', belongs to the caller at app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:751 and :844, which is what decides what a status means. Operation codes 'W' (:107) and 'Z' (:108) are declared in the linkage area and tested by no IF in any of the four paragraphs, and the program contains no WRITE and no REWRITE verb at all, so no write path exists to drive. This case drives only 'O' and 'R'; where a sibling does reach those two codes it asserts the silent no-op they actually produce rather than an implemented write, which is what preserving them unimplemented means (practice B5). Provenance (practice B12, risk R-A): these expected rather than tidied away (practice B5). Provenance (practice B12, risk R-A): these expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED and were NEVER captured from a COBOL execution, which AAP 0.7.6 proves impossible in this environment across eight independently verified blockers and 0.9.11 escalates for explicit confirmation - CBSTM03B cannot even be built here, since cobc refuses it because PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LK-M03B-AREA (:114) is a subprogram entry and not a -x main. They come from the line numbers cited above, from the byte offsets of app/cpy/COSTM01.CPY, and from app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL STEP010, whose OUTREC FIELDS=(1:263,16, 17:1,262, 279:279,50) was applied mechanically to rows 20 and 101 (0-based) of app/data/ASCII/dailytran.txt - source 263-278 to TRNX 1-16, source 1-262 to TRNX 17-278, source 279-328 to TRNX 279-328, leaving 329-350 blank-filled by SORT. Both rows carry card 0500024453765740, which is cardxref.txt row 0's XREF-CARD-NUM, so the seed is coherent with the other three DDs; they are seeded inline because TRNXFILE is a derived dataset with no ASCII fixture and the fixture count is fixed at nine. The trailing 'H' and '{' in TRNX-AMT are zoned sign overpunches on PIC S9(09)V99 ('{' = +0 through 'I' = +9), so the images denote +183.88 and +14.00 and are reproduced as bytes rather than normalised to a signed literal. The seed is byte-identical to case01's two rows, which script the OPEN alone, and to the first two of case03's three, which carry this story on to the second READ and the CLOSE - case03's third row exists so that its CLOSE can be shown to consume nothing. All byte content is US-ASCII, stated explicitly and never taken from the platform default (practice B8). HOW THE CALL SCRIPT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN HELD IN JAVA: the sequence of CALLs below used to live in a Java switch over this file's case identifier, which meant the case file did not describe the one thing it asserts - a subroutine whose entire contract is a DD name plus a one-character operation code IS its call sequence. Renumbering this file would have silently given it a different script, and a twenty-first case would have thrown from a default arm. unitStimulus.operationScript now carries it, one entry per CALL in issue order, each declaring LK-M03B-DD, the 88-level operation code from app/cbl/CBSTM03B.cbl:103-108, and where applicable LK-M03B-KEY and LK-M03B-KEY-LN. Two caller idioms are declared explicitly because the source distinguishes them: status '00' is the MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC every real call site issues, and its ABSENCE carries the previous call's status forward - the only way to observe a fall-through exit that assigns nothing new; primesRecordArea true is the MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT that app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L350, :L745 and :L834 issue, and its ABSENCE is the omission at :L857-860 that makes 'at end of file the record area is returned unchanged' an assertion with content. Every expected area image below was derived from this script by reading CBSTM03B's rules, never by running the Java.
